successCriterion: the locating trace answers whether expand was used and what it saw; VALID_REPRODUCTION is not the success criterion

evidenceAsymmetry.selectionLegality: The selected case is the only source-gate member that passed the five mechanical conditions. filtersNotApplied records that whether the defect crosses DI, AOP, or event graph edges was not a selection filter. The strength table below is interpretation background, not a selection rule.

expandUsed.reason: salespoint is a Spring framework itself, and the repair site PersistentAccountancy.java sits in a DI-dense area. That is favorable for the graph arm. A single favorable case does not generalize.

expandUnused.reason: If expand remains unused even under this favorable condition, the cause is locked to tool design or the locating prompt, not cohort composition.

limitations: n=1. This is a case study. It does not support statistical conclusions and must not be used for arm-to-arm comparison.
The model identifier has no dated weight pin; the vendor may change weights without renaming. Results are not a long-term reproducibility claim.
Training-data composition and knowledge cutoff are unpublished, so contamination against this GitBug-Java case cannot be bounded.
Formal runs depend on a locally mounted GitBug-Java tree for the issue body and revisions; public clone URLs plus this repository's frozen metadata are not enough to reproduce the run.

Three AGENT_BENCHMARK runs are stored regardless of downstream success or failure. Pipeline failures unrelated to locating (Docker, environment, transport) may be retried once and must be recorded; result-driven reruns are not permitted.
Localization coverage is an oracle-derived metric. It is reported after the run. It must not enter Generator Context, Generation Feedback, or locating_trace.
